Sarah — thanks for flagging this and sending the .ics. I took a quick look: the invite we sent was created in America/Los_Angeles (DTSTART;TZID=America/Los_Angeles). It looks like when it was forwarded in your routing tool it got normalized to a UTC start (DTSTART:20261202T100000Z) without a TZID, which can cause clients to interpret it as a floating UTC time.

Quick plan:
- I'll create a fresh invite explicitly pinned to America/Los_Angeles and include an explicit TZID block in the .ics.
- Adding Marissa and Diego to verify on Outlook/GCal and to confirm recipients in EU/APAC see the correct local time.
- If that doesn't resolve it, we can move the demo to 18:00 UTC (10:00 PST / 19:00 CET) which should be safer for APAC folks who are flexible.

For visibility I'm attaching a screenshot of the calendar header showing the Z label (screenshot-calendar-zulu-header.png). Sarah / Tim, please hold on accepting until we send the corrected invite — accepting now may pin the wrong local time for some attendees.

Sarah / Tim — I investigated the forwarded .ics and reproduced the bug. Summary:

- The original invite contained:
  BEGIN:VTIMEZONE
  TZID:America/Los_Angeles
  ...
  END:VTIMEZONE
  DTSTART;TZID=America/Los_Angeles:20261202T100000

- After your automation forwarded it, the TZID block was dropped and the DTSTART was converted to UTC (DTSTART:20261202T100000Z). Some clients (notably older GCal routing hooks and certain Exchange->GCal flows) treat that as an absolute UTC instant and display the label "Z" in the header; others treat it as a floating time. That mismatch explains why APAC recipients saw midnight.

What's done:
- I created a replacement invite explicitly pinned to America/Los_Angeles and exported a fresh .ics (bw-demo-fixed.ics).
- I also created a second invite pinned to UTC/Coordinated Universal Time for customers who prefer a timezone-agnostic anchor and sent a calendar note explaining accept/decline behavior.
- Sarah: please decline the original invite and accept only the attached bw-demo-fixed.ics so your attendees get the correct local conversion. We also added a short note in the description: "If your calendar shows UTC/Z or floating times, re-import this invite and accept the one marked 'Fixed - America/Los_Angeles'."

Next steps / ask:
- Sarah / Tim: confirm once you accept the fixed invite.
- Ethan: can we add a one-line troubleshooting note in the demo confirmation email explaining the forwarder issue so Bellwether's scheduling automation doesn't re-forward the original?

Thanks —
